message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated American composers across different eras:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works |
|----------|-------------|---------------|
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | Late Romantic/Patriotic marches | “Stars and Stripes Forever,” “The Washington Post” |
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz‑influenced classical | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris” |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Mid‑20th‑century neoclassicism | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Broadway & symphonic | “West Side Story,” “Candide” |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Modernist/neo‑romantic | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915” |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | “Glassworks,” “Einstein on the Beach” |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film score composer | “Star Wars,” “Indiana Jones,” “Jurassic Park” |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains” |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Early modernist | “The Unanswered Question,” “Concord Sonata” |

These figures have shaped American music from patriotic marches to jazz-infused symphonies, film scores, and avant‑garde minimalism.
